origin: Single motivated change from v1, per Researcher review (strategies/day_trading/nfp_fade/v1/review.md, 2026-09-23). v1's calendar trigger (computed 'first Friday of month, days 1-7') was investigated against all 59 v1 in-sample trade dates and confirmed to have fired zero wrong-day trades in that sample, BUT was separately confirmed to silently miss real BLS NFP release events that fall outside the first-Friday window (Jan 2020's real release was Jan 10, not the computed Jan 3; Jan 2021's real release was Jan 8, not the computed Jan 1, which is also a market holiday). This is the ONLY change in v2: everything else (measurement window, threshold, SL/TP, hold time, sizing, pairs, safety rules) is byte-for-byte identical to v1, deliberately, per this project's house rule against bundling multiple changes into one refinement.
thesis: Unchanged from v1 -- see v1/spec.json for the full thesis writeup (Street Smarts / Raschke & Connors 1996 'News Strategy' fading the initial overreaction to a scheduled 8:30am ET release, applied to NFP specifically).

calendar_trigger.rule: actual historical BLS Employment Situation (NFP) release date, from a hardcoded per-month lookup table -- NOT computed from a day-of-month rule
calendar_trigger.change_reasoning: v1's known_simplification (first Friday of month, days 1-7) is confirmed correct for every one of v1's 59 actual in-sample trades (see v1/review.md Part 1 -- no wrong-day trade found), but confirmed to silently SKIP real NFP events when the true BLS release falls outside days 1-7 (Jan 2020: real release Jan 10, rule computed Jan 3, zero trade fired that month; Jan 2021: real release Jan 8, rule computed Jan 1 -- a market holiday -- zero trade fired). This under-samples an already low-frequency (~12/year/pair) event-anchored strategy for no reason other than an avoidable approximation error. Fixing it does not change any other mechanic -- it only recovers months v1 silently dropped, growing the sample using the exact same locked entry/exit logic.
calendar_trigger.implementation: Hardcoded table, one release date per calendar month, covering 2017.01 through 2025.12 (full in-sample + out-of-sample window) -- explicitly NOT MT5's CalendarValueHistory() API. v1's spec deliberately avoided MT5 Strategy Tester's live economic-calendar feed as 'unreliable/absent per project instruction'; that concern is not being revisited here without a dedicated feasibility check, so a static table (same pattern as this strategy's own DST table in dates.md, and gotobi's gotobi-day table) is used instead.
calendar_trigger.sourcing_requirement: The table MUST be built from BLS's own published 'Schedule of Releases' archive (bls.gov, archived year-by-year release calendars for the Employment Situation report), not approximated or inferred from the first-Friday rule. Two exceptions are already confirmed and MUST be reflected exactly: January 2020 = 2020.01.10 (not 2020.01.03); January 2021 = 2021.01.08 (not 2021.01.01). Every other 2017-2022 month was checked against 'first Friday' in v1/review.md and found to match, but EA Coder should still source real dates for all of them directly (not copy the first-Friday computation) since the table needs to be authoritative on its own, and 2023-2025 (out-of-sample) has NOT been checked by Researcher at all and must be sourced fresh, not inferred.
calendar_trigger.fallback_if_month_missing_from_table: if a month is genuinely missing from the sourced table (should not happen for 2017-2025, a fully elapsed historical range), skip that month's trade entirely -- do not fall back to the old first-Friday computation, which would reintroduce the exact problem being fixed.
calendar_trigger.note_broker_clock_conversion: unchanged from v1 -- the US-DST x broker-DST algorithm in dates.md still applies to whatever release DATE comes out of the new table; only the date-selection mechanism changes, not the intraday time-of-day conversion, which Backtester already spot-checked and confirmed correct to the minute in v1.

entry: unchanged from v1 -- see v1/spec.json for measurement_window (T+0 to T+10min), MinSpikeSizePipsFloor=15, MinSpikeVsAvgMultiplier=1.2, SpikeHistoryWindowEvents=12, MinHistoryToAdapt=6, skip_conditions. Do not modify any of these values.
stop_loss: unchanged from v1 -- spike size * SLMultiplier (1.0).
take_profit: unchanged from v1 -- spike size * TPMultiplier (1.3).
exit: unchanged from v1 -- 60-minute hold backstop after the measurement window closes, end_of_day_flat_hour_server=22.
safety_rules: unchanged from v1 -- see v1/spec.json (consecutive_loss_pause threshold=6, daily_loss_stop_percent=5.0, max_drawdown_stop_percent=15.0, never_scale_up_after_loss, max_one_position_per_pair_per_event, live_account_opt_in_required).
tunable_parameters_to_sweep: none for v2, same as v1 -- this is a data-correctness fix, not a parameter search.

demo_criteria.rationale: unchanged from v1 -- low-frequency calendar-event strategy, min_days is the binding constraint, not trade count. Not adjusted despite v1's thin 59-trade result, per house rule against moving the bar after seeing results -- if v2's corrected calendar still can't clear this, that is itself a finding, not a reason to lower the bar.

expected_outcome_note: This is a completeness fix, not a signal redesign -- expect a modestly larger sample (a small number of recovered months per pair), not a dramatically different one. Do not expect this alone to flip GBPUSD.r's or USDJPY's v1 results; its purpose is to get the combined sample closer to a size where PF/win rate are actually statistically decidable, per v1/review.md's closing note. If the corrected sample is still well under the 200-trade bar and results remain mixed/flat, the next honest conclusion is likely 'structurally too low-frequency for this account's cost profile to reach statistical confidence' -- not another mechanism tweak.
